headline: Transformers decode nanopore raw currents for modification and tRNA calling
label: Deep Learning Nanopore Signals
summary: Deep models now read raw nanopore currents directly, bypassing basecalling for modification, tRNA, and taxonomic inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning applied directly to raw biological measurements, with three of five items working on nanopore data. Brieno tokenizes raw nanopore signals via residual vector quantization and pretrains a Transformer on 118M reads, targeting species identification, basecalling, and methylation. RawMod applies a transformer to raw-signal pileups for control-free, modification-agnostic detection of DNA base modifications. A separate model classifies E. coli tRNA species from direct RNA ionic currents without basecalling, reporting 98.2% accuracy. DeepHel applies multi-stage deep learning to Helitron transposon annotation, benchmarked against HiTE and HELIANO on five eukaryotic genomes, while DeepEST assigns GO terms to bacterial proteins from expression, operon-aware gene location, and predicted structures. What is new is the move toward pretrained, modification-agnostic models that reduce reliance on basecalling and matched controls.
